title: Brief special meeting authorizes closed session
subtitle: Land acknowledgement, Indigenous History Month and Pride Month statements, and by-law confirmation of council proceedings
overview: Kitchener City Council held a short special meeting on June 13, 2024. It ran from about 4:39 p.m. to 4:45 p.m. and was chaired by the Mayor. There were no disclosures of pecuniary interest, no delegations and no mayoral business.

Council authorized a closed session to follow the meeting. It covered two matters: one solicitor-client privilege matter, and one solicitor-client privilege and litigation or potential litigation matter {{vote:m1}}. The minutes publicly report nothing further about these items, and no decisions from the closed session are recorded.
Council also gave third reading to the by-law confirming its actions and proceedings for the day (By-law 2024-115) {{vote:m2}}. That is a routine step.

The meeting opened with a land acknowledgement and statements marking National Indigenous History Month and Pride Month. The statements described City work on reconciliation, including plans for an Indigenous gathering space at Huron Natural Area, and the Progress Pride flag raised at City Hall for June.

decisions.detail: Council authorized a closed session after the meeting to consider one solicitor-client privilege matter and one solicitor-client privilege and litigation or potential litigation matter under the Municipal Act, 2001.

debate: No debate took place. The motions were moved, seconded and carried by voice vote without discussion.
No delegations were registered, so there were no concerns from residents or other speakers.

The only substantive remarks were the Mayor's statements for National Indigenous History Month and Pride Month. They described the City's reconciliation work, including intercultural training, the RISE Fund and a planned Indigenous gathering space at Huron Natural Area, and its commitment to an inclusive city.
